dt-maturity.app

Digital Transformation Maturity Tool

Most digital-maturity assessments are a one-time survey — a snapshot an organization takes once and files away. This app treats the assessment as something to come back to: retake it every quarter, and see immediately whether the initiatives you funded actually moved the score, dimension by dimension.

Express node:sqlite JWT auth Chart.js Tailwind CSS English / العربية · RTL
trend view
zero build tools
node:sqlite over better-sqlite3. The native alternative needs ~6GB of build tools before anyone can even run the project. Node's built-in SQLite module needed none — npm install && npm start was worth more than the marginal performance.
real RTL
Logical properties, not translated strings. Layout uses start/end instead of hardcoded left/right, so switching to Arabic actually mirrors navigation, forms, and the Likert scale — not just the copy.
caught in testing
The trend chart's time axis stays left-to-right even in RTL. An early version mirrored it for consistency, but a real usability pass showed a genuine improvement (2.00 → 3.63) reading as decline once the axis reversed. Fixed by keeping time strictly chronological, regardless of text direction.

security-auditor.app

Security Headers & TLS Auditor

Paste any public URL and get an instant security posture report — HTTP security headers, TLS/certificate health, transport enforcement, and cookie flags — scored and graded, with concrete fixes for anything missing. Re-scan the same domain later and see whether it actually improved. Built alongside the maturity tool as a second, security-flavored take on the same "assess it, track it over time" idea — this one leaning on penetration-testing coursework instead of survey design.

Node.js Express node:sqlite Chart.js No auth — domain-keyed
scan history
SSRF-hardened
Connects to a validated IP, never a re-resolved hostname. A tool that scans whatever URL a user pastes is a textbook SSRF risk — it already refused cloud-metadata IPs, loopback, and private ranges, but the DNS lookup used to check a hostname and the connection that followed were still two separate steps, open to a DNS-rebinding swap in between. Closed that gap by resolving once, connecting straight to the validated IP, and passing the original hostname only through TLS SNI and the HTTP Host header.
no login
History keyed by domain, not by account. Security scanners like securityheaders.com and SSL Labs are used ad hoc — paste a URL, get a report, no account needed. This one has no auth at all; scan history is keyed by the domain itself, a deliberate contrast to the maturity tool's per-organization login.
caught in testing
The rate limiter wasn't actually a hard gate. Live re-testing turned up an inconsistency: rapid repeat scans of the same domain sometimes returned a generic connection error instead of the intended "try again in Ns" response — the check was racing the scan instead of blocking it first. Fixed by moving the rate-limit check before any network call runs, so a repeat scan is rejected the same way every time.

lamma-trivia.onrender.com

Lamma — Live Trivia Game

لمّة (Arabic for a casual gathering of friends) is real-time, Kahoot-style trivia built for groups of adults: one big screen hosts the round while everyone else joins from their own phone with a room code or QR scan. Scoring rewards speed and confidence over lucky guesses, and an AI-assisted bank of 650+ questions across 20 categories means the same group of friends can play again next month without hitting a repeat.

Node.js Express Socket.io node:sqlite Arabic-first · RTL
host lobby
host holds the state
The big screen is the source of truth; phones are just input. The host client owns the room, the question order, and the timer over Socket.io — players' phones only ever send an answer event and render their own score. That split is what makes joining as simple as scanning a QR code or typing a six-character room code, with no login for anyone.
speed over luck
Scoring rewards how fast you answer, not just whether you're right. Points scale down from 1000 to a 300 floor based on how much of the time window is left, plus a streak bonus of up to +50% for consecutive correct answers — and a wrong answer costs nothing, so no one stops playing after one bad guess.
free hosting, stateless by design
The free host tier sleeps after 15 minutes idle, and node:sqlite is a local file that resets on every cold start. That's fine here on purpose: the question bank loads fresh from bundled JSON at boot instead of depending on a persisted database, so a sleep-and-wake cycle never loses content — only a good, free, always-there link matters for a portfolio piece.
